method: Interval geometry rebuilt with the compact-v1 chain rule and measured against the nearest active OpenStreetMap railway way of the line's own type (service tracks excluded) via Overpass; long intervals sampled at 20 points plus every vertex within 150 m of a sample. A = consistent (median well inside the kind limit, no localised excursion); C = only OSM's tunnel approximation disagrees. B (package wrong) and D (not measured) are never released.

packageBoundMethod: Rows tagged "method": "package-bound" were NOT re-measured against OpenStreetMap: that session had no Overpass access and no local source tree. They are released on evidence already in this repository. (R1) The package's own per-line maxDeviationMeters - measured at every vertex against the independent reference, and therefore an upper bound on this interval's own worst deviation - is within 1.5x the profile limit, the same bar every A row above states; worstAt says whether that number belongs to this interval or to another one. (R2) The line's unmatched count is 0, so no drawn vertex is more than 400 m from surveyed track. (R3) The rebuilt interval shows none of this project's known failure modes: no chord across a curve, no detour, no internal reversal, no self-overlap, no vertex jump past the profile's densify cap, and both endpoints exactly on their station anchors. (R4) It is not an interval the Overpass run measured and rejected. Where another line in the packages runs the same corridor, its vertex-by-vertex agreement is recorded in peerMedianMetres / peerP95Metres / peerMaxMetres together with that peer's own geometry source and recorded maxDeviationMeters. Applied line-wide this rule refuses both intervals the Overpass run rejected as B, so it contradicts no measured verdict in this table. These rows stay listed in notMeasured, which records what the Overpass run covered. Full working, and the three intervals that stay withheld for want of that feed: app/public/rail/na-2025-blocked-intervals.md.
